questions.q: What is a Log Analytics workspace?
options: A dashboard of pinned charts
The container that stores ingested log tables and is queried with KQL
A type of Azure Monitor alert
A billing report for Azure Monitor usage
questions.explain: A workspace holds the tables (AppRequests, AppExceptions, AzureActivity, etc.) that KQL queries run against. You must scope a query to a workspace before running it.

questions.q: In the query `AppRequests | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h) | summarize avg(DurationMs) by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)`, what does `bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)` do?
options: Deletes requests older than 5 minutes
Groups rows into 5-minute time buckets for the aggregation
Limits the query to exactly 5 rows
Converts the table to 5 minutes of retention
questions.explain: bin() buckets TimeGenerated values into fixed-size intervals — here, 5-minute buckets — so summarize can compute an aggregate per bucket instead of one aggregate for the whole time range.

questions.q: What does the `render timechart` operator do?
options: Deletes the chart from the workspace
Exports the query to a Python script
Draws the query's tabular result as a time chart inline in the query editor
Schedules the query to run automatically every hour
questions.explain: render is the last step in a KQL pipeline that turns the result set into a visual chart without leaving the query editor.

questions.q: Can you turn a KQL query's output into a chart without using `render` in the query itself?
options: No, render is the only way to visualize results
Yes — the results pane lets you switch any tabular result to a chart after running the query
Only if the query uses the summarize operator
Only for queries against AppExceptions
questions.explain: The Log Analytics results pane includes a chart toggle that works on any tabular output, independent of whether the query itself used render.

questions.q: In the workflow this lesson describes, what's the relationship between metrics and KQL log queries during an incident?
options: Metrics and logs are unrelated and used in separate incidents
Metrics tell you when something changed; KQL log queries tell you what specifically happened
KQL replaces the need for metrics entirely
Metrics are only used for billing, not incident response
questions.explain: A metric spike (seen in Metrics Explorer) tells you when latency changed. A KQL query against the request/exception tables for that window tells you exactly what happened and why.
